briefing.headline: Three free transfers and three broken assets: move Konsa out, and the Palmer-to-Saka swap is the one that actually buys points — then captain Fernandes, not your injured captain.

do.why: Konsa is in your starting XI projecting 0.98 points: 39% chance of playing, 20 minutes in his last outing, an unspecified injury at 75%, and absent from Rotowire's predicted Arsenal XI. N.Williams has played 90/90 at 100% likelihood and projects 19.9 over five against Konsa's 10.8 — a 9.1-point gain for one free transfer, and it drops you to two Arsenal players, which is what makes the Saka move legal.

A near-exact price swap that gains 2.0 this week (6.01 v 4.00) and 9.5 over five (28.3 v 18.8), and removes a muscular injury rated 75%. Both are first on penalties, so the model's missing penalty-taker bonus doesn't favour either. Palmer is 24.4% owned and Saka 15.3%, so you are taking on a little price risk for a clear projection gain, not giving anything up in template terms.

do.action: Change the captain off Palmer to B.Fernandes, and make Mbeumo vice
do.why: Palmer projects 4.00 with a 75% fitness flag; Fernandes projects 7.17 at home to Tottenham (FDR 2) with 90/90 minutes, 100% play and penalties. Mbeumo (6.57) is the backup in the same fixture, which is fine — if Fernandes is a late withdrawal Mbeumo still kicks off.

do.action: Start De Cuyper and Gomez; bench Konsa (or his replacement) and João Pedro
do.why: Your bench currently holds De Cuyper (4.10) and Gomez (4.17) while Konsa (0.98) starts. Even before transfers that is roughly three points thrown away for free. Post-transfers the best XI is Raya; Calafiori 4.66, Thiaw 4.10, De Cuyper 4.10; Fernandes 7.17, Mbeumo 6.57, Saka 6.01, Tavernier 4.45, Gomez 4.17; Thiago 4.80, Barry 4.61 — with Guéhi (3.38, away at Liverpool, FDR 4) and Calvert-Lewin (3.68, away at Arsenal, FDR 5) the unlucky ones on the bench.

consider.action: Use the third free transfer on João Pedro (£7.7m) → Barry (EVE, £5.7m)
consider.why: For: João Pedro projects 0.99 this week and 10.1 over five — 28% chance of playing, 15 minutes last time out, a knee injury at 75% and no place in the predicted Chelsea XI. Barry plays (97%, 86/90), is on Everton's penalties, projects 20.1 over five, and the swap banks £2.0m. Against: 63.6% of all managers own João Pedro, a 75% flag is a doubt rather than an absence, and the minutes model is known to drag an injured player's five-week number down by projecting his recent absence forward — if he starts at home to Bournemouth that 10.1 is simply wrong. The deciding point is that waiting costs nothing: using two transfers leaves you two next week, so you can watch the team news and still act in GW7.

consider.action: Starting Guéhi ahead of De Cuyper
consider.why: For: Guéhi is your £6.0m defender with 21.0 over five and only drops out this week because City travel to Liverpool (FDR 4) — benching him on a 0.72 projected difference is noise-level churn. Against: the 0.72 is free and De Cuyper has the softer draw. Either is defensible; don't agonise.

ignore.why: He is 74.0% owned overall and the biggest single rank risk you carry, but at £15.6m with £0.5m in the bank he cannot be funded. The only route is selling Fernandes, and Haaland's 32.6 over five against Fernandes's 31.0 is 1.6 points, which would be wiped out several times over by the £4.5m midfielder you'd be forced to buy and by losing your captaincy option. Note it as the risk you're carrying, don't act on it this week.

ignore.action: The cheap high-value defenders — Thomas (COV, £4.0m, 17.4 over five) and Davis (IPS, £4.0m, 17.3)
ignore.why: Both are flagged thin evidence: 437 and 450 minutes respectively, all of it this season. Those projections are an extrapolation from five matches, and you don't need the £1.0m they'd release.
No blank or double in GW6 and your bench after transfers reads Kelleher 3.52, N.Williams 3.93, Guéhi 3.38 and Calvert-Lewin 3.68 — a Bench Boost there is worth roughly a normal bench, not a chip.

ignore.action: Panicking at the overall rank of 4,924,791
ignore.why: Your wildcard from the first set is already gone, so there is no reset available. Over-trading now, with three live doubts in the squad, is how you end up taking hits in GW7 and GW8. Make the clear moves and keep a transfer in hand.

captain.why: Fernandes projects 7.17 at home to Tottenham (FDR 2), highest in your squad, with penalties and 90/90 minutes; Mbeumo is 6.57 in the same match and takes the armband if Fernandes drops out. The ownership reality: Haaland is 74.0% owned overall and is the field's default captain, and you don't have him — so you are already captaining differently to most of the game whatever you do. That is a rank bet you cannot avoid this week, which is a reason to take the highest-projecting option you own rather than hedging. Top-10k ownership and captaincy are withheld this week, so there is nothing reliable to say about elite consensus.

briefing.chips: No chip this week. Free Hit and Bench Boost both remain from the first set, and both expire at the GW19 deadline (2 January 2027) — that is thirteen gameweeks away, which is comfortable but not infinite. Hold them for a blank or double; a Bench Boost on this bench would score about what a bench scores.
risks: The Rotowire set covers all 10 matches, so Konsa and João Pedro being absent from their predicted XIs is meaningful — but it is still a prediction, and the model pulls a player left out 70% of the way towards not starting. If either is named, their one-point projections are badly understated.

Palmer passing his fitness test and hauling at home to Bournemouth is the obvious way the Saka move looks bad in a week. He is first on penalties and the model has no penalty-taker bonus, so his ceiling is above his 4.00.

Selling prices are assumed to be current prices. Your wildcard was only in GW4 so purchase prices are recent and any shortfall should be small, but check in the app before confirming three moves against a £0.5m bank.
Saka's 82/90 minutes and 98% play assume no European rotation; the bundle carries no midweek schedule, so that is unmodelled.
If João Pedro returns to the Chelsea XI and you have sold him, you are short of a widely owned forward (63.6%) with no wildcard left to correct course cheaply.
